He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
This is a case of online fraud.
According to the FIR, on 05.06.2023, the informant received a telephone call.
The caller introduced himself as the nephew of the informant and demanded Rs.8 Lakh conveying that he has stuck in Canada and he has to return some money.

Believing the caller,
the informant deposited the money.
When more demand was raised, the informant would sense the fraud.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that there is no evidence against the applicant; he is not a previous convict; the applicant is not connected with any account, in which the money was deposited.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that a mobile number was recovered from the applicant and it was found that the SIM through which the informant was called had run from that mobile number.
It is argued that it was so established through IMEI number.

Although, it is argued on behalf of the State that when arrested the applicant told it to the police that he could change the IMEI number by using the different patterns, which he, in fact, demonstrated also, which is so stated in para 5 of the counter affidavit.
